reason: Boatlike = boat-shaped, the same as the rules for boat-shaped, navicular and cymbiform (PATO:0002426 scaphoid).
States that bracts are absent beside the fruit or receptacle, like the 'ebracteate' rule. 'Lateral' only says where the missing bracts would be.
A fruit surface marked by a network of ridges, some running crosswise. FLOPO reticulate already covers networks of ridges on fruits and seeds.

label: epicortical
definition: A positional quality inhering in a root of a parasitic plant by virtue of the root's running along the outer surface of the host's bark, from which it sends haustoria into the host. NOTE: Botany-specific (mistletoes, Loranthaceae and Viscaceae); sibling of FLOPO:0991036 aerial and FLOPO:0991035 subterranean.
reason: A real, well-defined position of mistletoe roots on the host. No PATO or FLOPO position term covers it.
Two shape values joined into one word: a continuum between globose and ovoid, not a term of its own.
A comparison of length with another part ('equaling or exceeding the …'). It needs the second part named and is the equality case of pattern 10.
Almost umbel-like. The value is umbelliform, with value_qualifier 'sub' as in pattern 01 (approximate value).

label: follicle-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of a follicle, a dry fruit derived from a single carpel that opens along one side. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991200 bract-like and PATO:0002457 leaf-like, worded as they are; PO_0030105 follicle fruit is the part itself.
reason: The fruit resembles a follicle without being called one. This is the same case as the existing '-like' shape classes.
A count: each seed has one plant embryo (PO_0009009). Polyembryonic is the same pattern with a count above one.
Scabrellate = slightly scabrous. FLOPO scabrous already lists scaberulous and scabridulous as related synonyms.
In floras 'compressed' means flattened (see flora_union_pairs.tsv), not PATO condensed. 'Sub-' becomes value_qualifier 'sub' as in pattern 01.
A plant growing into a low convex mound has a cushion habit. This matches the earlier rule 'cushion-shaped' = pulvinate.
'Perispore surface without folds' = not folded. The bearer 'perispore' needs its own bearer rule.
A multiheaded caudex divides into several crowns, i.e. a branched caudex (stem by rule C252).
The colour of the dried specimen (black) with a negation. This is pattern 06 plus negation, not a term.
Withered = shrunken and dried. PATO:0002460 shriveled is defined as smaller and contracted through loss of moisture. The leaf position 'proximal' goes to pattern 04.

Cicatrose twigs carry many scars, e.g. leaf scars. PATO:0002421 cicatricial ('having the characteristic of a cicatrix') fits better than PATO:0001850 scarred, which means replacement of injured tissue.
Adventive means introduced, not native. That is the plant's distribution status, not a quality of the plant.
A faint yellow tinge. The value is yellow with value_qualifier 'approximately', as pattern 01 does for colour words like 'greenish'.
A plant that climbs by clinging roots. FLOPO climbing explicitly includes clinging, as do the rules for lianescent and scrambling.
Two values joined: minutely pilose hairs (FLOPO:0991048 pilose, qualifier 'sub') that lie appressed (FLOPO:0991064). Strigulose is not the same, because it implies stiff hairs.
Slightly exserted. The value is exserted with value_qualifier 'sub' as in pattern 01.
Silky is an exact synonym of sericeous. 'Short' only describes hair length.
A seed bent out of its plane, not along a regular axis. Torsioned (twisted about an axis) is too specific.
Two shape values in one word: discoid (PATO:0001874) and ring shaped (PATO:0002539, synonym annular), describing the apex of a nutlet or beak.
An obscure word with no stable glossary meaning. The source itself marks it uncertain ('?pseudogemmulate').
Two values joined: almost linear (PATO:0001199, qualifier 'sub') and elongated (PATO:0001154).
Vernation noncircinate = young leaves not coiled. This is the negation of PATO:0001964 circinate.
Trichomes with several rays are stellate (exact synonym of PATO:0002065). 'Several' is too vague for a count, as in the earlier rejection of 'several'.
Semirotund = half-round in outline (sepals, stipules, leaf base lobes). PATO:0002232 semicircular is the shape of half a circle.
